Module 1 · Welcome & who we are

Welcome to WoodBClean

The story behind why we exist, what we stand for, and what it actually means to represent this business from day one.

💡
Why this mattersNon-solicitation protects you too. If you build your own client base from WoodBClean clients and something goes wrong on a job — a chemical damage claim, an injury — you have none of WoodBClean's insurance backing you. Operating through WoodBClean means you are protected.

How WoodBClean started

Bonnie Wood built this business from her name — and from a genuine frustration with the way cleaning was being done.

She was working in hospitality, meeting every kind of client a cleaning business could dream of — homeowners, landlords, property managers, builders. She was having real conversations, building real relationships, and hearing the same complaints over and over: cleaners who showed up late, did half the job, or didn't show up at all. Facebook groups full of stories about people who cleaned fast because it was quick cash — and left clients with a mess they had to deal with themselves.

Bonnie knew she could do it differently. So she did.

"WoodBClean — because it would be clean if you got WoodBClean." That's not just a tagline. That's a promise. Every job we take on, every door we walk through, we are making that promise to someone.

Why organic and Australian-made

WoodBClean doesn't use conventional cleaning chemicals — and there's a real reason for that, not just a marketing one.

Conventional cleaning products are made from petrochemicals — derivatives of crude oil. They work, but they leave residue on surfaces, they go down drains into waterways, and they sit in the air in the homes of the clients we're cleaning for. Babies crawl on those floors. Pets lick those surfaces. People with asthma breathe that air.

We use the Clean Like A Pro range — an Australian-owned, Australian-made product line created by professional bond cleaners who had the same frustration we did. Powerful enough to do the job properly. Designed to not poison the environments we're cleaning.

When a client books WoodBClean, they're trusting us with their home. Using products that are safe for their family is part of that trust.

What we've built

WoodBClean services South East Queensland across residential homes, Airbnbs and short-term rentals, new builds, bond and sellers cleans, and mould treatment. Our team is a mix of employees and subcontractors — and every single one of us is held to the same standard.

We are not a volume business. We don't win by doing more jobs than anyone else. We win by being the business that clients call back, refer to their friends, and trust with their front door key.

That reputation is built by you — every single day.
"The very most important element to being a cleaner at WoodBClean is common sense. See something that needs fixing? Fix it. Don't walk past a problem because it wasn't on the list." — Bonnie

Who we are

WoodBClean is a professional cleaning company serving South East Queensland — but we are much more than that. We are a support network, a connection, and a community built around one simple belief: when our team members thrive, our clients feel the difference.

We service residential homes, short-term rentals, businesses, government buildings, and new builds across South East Queensland. Our team includes both employees and subcontractors — and every one of us holds ourselves to the same standard of professionalism, care, and respect.

You are not just a cleaner. You are a trained professional who people trust to enter their home, their office, or their workplace. That means something. We want every member of this team to feel proud of the work they do and supported in building a genuinely great career.

WoodBClean is a community

We believe in improving not just the spaces we clean — but the lives of the people in our team. WoodBClean actively supports our team members to grow, connect, and succeed.
Team connection
You are part of a team that looks out for each other. Bonnie is always reachable and always in your corner.
Career growth
Clear pathways from new starter to specialist. Your training and effort directly open new doors and higher pay.
Real support
We connect team members with accountants, insurance brokers, and support services. You are not on your own.
Inclusive team
Team members from all backgrounds are welcome. 23 languages available in this portal — because your success matters.
If you are ever unsure about something — whether it is about your pay, your rights, your tax, or anything else — ask Bonnie. We will find the right answer or connect you with the right person.

Our 4 core values

Integrity
Always honest — with clients, with teammates, whether or not anyone is watching
Excellence
We never cut corners. Leave when the job meets standard, not when the clock says
Respect
For every environment we work in — homes, businesses, government buildings, and new builds — and for every person we work alongside
Safety first
Your wellbeing matters above all else. No job is worth a shortcut on safety

What these values mean day-to-day

Integrity means if you break something, tell Bonnie immediately. If you are running late, communicate. If a client offers cash on the side, decline and report it. It means being the same person whether or not anyone is watching.

Excellence means you do not leave a job because the clock says it is time — you leave because the job is done to standard. Check your work before you walk out the door. Ask yourself: would I be happy coming home to this?

Respect means treating every environment we work in — whether it is a family home, a government building, a business, or a brand new build — with the same care and professionalism. No going through drawers, no moving personal items without need, no making unnecessary noise. Respect applies equally to the people we work alongside, our clients, and the spaces we are trusted to work in.

Safety first means you never rush a chemical mix, never skip PPE because it is uncomfortable, and never push through fatigue to finish faster. A safe team is a productive team.

On-site conduct — what we always do

Knock before entering any roomEven if you know the client is not home. This is professional habit.
Wear your uniform at all times on siteClean, presentable, and identifiable as a WoodBClean professional.
Keep phone use strictly work-relatedPhotos and job communication only. Put your phone away unless needed.
Greet clients warmly and professionallyHi, I am [name] from WoodBClean, we are here to get started.
Report anything unusual to BonnieDamage, hazards, anything that does not seem right — report it, do not ignore it.

What we never do

Bring personal visitors to a job siteNo friends, family, or guests. This is a client private space.
Go through personal belongingsDrawers, cabinets, wardrobes — never. You are there to clean.
Discuss wages or payments with colleagues on siteWhat you earn is a private matter between you and Bonnie.
Take photos of client personal propertyJob documentation photos only. Never photograph personal items or valuables.
Post about clients or jobs on social mediaNo client addresses, property photos, or job details ever shared online.
Make unnecessary noiseLoud music, personal calls on speaker — be mindful. You are a guest in someone home.

When a client is unhappy — what to do

1
Listen without interrupting
Let them speak fully. Do not get defensive. Just listen.
2
Acknowledge — Thank you for letting me know
You do not have to agree with them to acknowledge how they feel.
3
For something small you can fix — fix it immediately
Then check back: Is that better for you?
4
For anything significant — I will pass this to Bonnie who will contact you today
Then call Bonnie immediately. Never make promises without her approval.
5
Never argue — even if you are right
Stay calm, stay professional, escalate. That is what Bonnie is there for.

What your first week at WoodBClean looks like

Your first week is about learning, understanding, and building the foundation before you step into a client's home independently. Here's what to expect:
1
This training program — all 16 modules
Work through each module in order. Don't rush it. The quiz at the end of each module confirms you've understood it before you move on.
2
Shadow an experienced WoodBClean cleaner
You'll go on a real job alongside a team member. Watch, ask questions, and pay attention to the details you wouldn't get from reading alone.
3
Learn the products and equipment
Know every product in the Clean Like A Pro range — what it does, what it's used on, and how it's diluted. Module 3 and 5 cover this in depth.
4
Complete your Module 1 readiness photo
Send Bonnie your photo on WhatsApp. That's your green light to move into your first supervised job.
If you have questions during your first week — ask Bonnie. No question is too small. A question asked once prevents a mistake that costs everyone.

Why key handling is so important

When a client gives WoodBClean a key, they are placing enormous trust in us. A lost or misused key is not just an inconvenience — it is a serious security breach that can cost the client money, damage our reputation, and create real legal liability. There are no exceptions to these rules.

The key handling process — every single time

1
Sign the key out
Record your full name, date, time, and job address in the key register before taking the key. Every time.
2
Keep the key on your person on site
The key stays in your pocket at all times while on site. Never leave it on a bench, in a door lock, or unattended.
3
Sign the key back in immediately after the job
Return to the register as soon as the job is complete. Record the time.
4
Return key to secure storage
Keys go back to the designated key safe. Never stored in your personal bag, car, or home overnight unless specifically approved by Bonnie.

If a key is lost — 4 steps immediately

1
Stop and retrace your steps thoroughly
Check pockets, kit bag, vehicle, and everywhere on site. Take a full 5 minutes.
2
Call Bonnie immediately — not after the job
Do not wait. Do not finish the job first. Call the moment you believe a key is lost.
3
Do not contact the client yourself
Bonnie handles all client communication in these situations.
4
Complete a written incident report the same day
Your manager will provide the form. Must be submitted the same day.
Real scenario
You finish a job and are driving home. You reach into your pocket and realise you do not have the client key. You are already 10 minutes away.
Correct response: Pull over safely. Call Bonnie immediately — before going back, before doing anything else. Bonnie will advise whether to return or if the key has been found. Complete an incident report the same day regardless of the outcome.

What is non-solicitation?

Non-solicitation means you agree not to approach WoodBClean clients — directly or indirectly — to offer your own cleaning services, or the services of any other cleaning company, either while you work here or for a defined period after you leave.

This applies to both employees and subcontractors. Clients are introduced to you through WoodBClean. Approaching them privately is a breach of trust and of your agreement.

What counts as solicitation — all prohibited

I do private cleans on weekends — here is my numberOffering your own services directly to a WoodBClean client in any form.
My mate runs a cleaning company — I can get you a better dealReferring WoodBClean clients to a competing business.
Leaving your personal card or contact details at a client propertyAny form of self-promotion at a client premises.
Connecting with clients on social media to promote your servicesUsing contact details obtained through work to market to clients personally.
If a client approaches you and asks for your personal contact details to book you privately — politely decline and let Bonnie know. You are not in trouble for reporting it. You are in trouble if you agree to it.
WoodBClean client property
A typical WoodBClean property — residential home, Brisbane. Every client who books WoodBClean is trusting someone with their most private space.

Who books WoodBClean

Our clients come from every corner of the market — and what they all have in common is one thing: they want the job done properly, without any hassle. That's it. No drama, no excuses, no having to follow up. Just arrive, do exceptional work, and leave the space transformed.
🏠
Homeowners and families
Often eco-conscious — they chose WoodBClean specifically because of our organic products. Some have young children or pets who are sensitive to chemicals. Your product choices and the way you communicate matter deeply to them.
🏢
Property managers and landlords
They are time-poor and managing multiple properties. They need reliability above everything. If you say you'll be there at 8am, be there at 7:55. If something's wrong, tell them through Bonnie — not a surprise.
🛏️
Airbnb and short-stay hosts
Their income depends on their review score. A guest arriving to a poorly prepared property can mean a 1-star review that costs the host hundreds of dollars. Your work directly impacts someone's livelihood.
🔨
Builders and developers
They have tight handover deadlines and are handing a property to someone who's spending hundreds of thousands of dollars. Attention to detail and the ability to work in a professional environment are non-negotiable.
📦
Tenants moving out
Often stressed, often under time pressure, and their bond deposit is on the line. A bond clean callback is not just an inconvenience — it can cost them real money. Our standard protects them.

What every client is trusting us with

Every client who gives WoodBClean a key or a door code is trusting us with the most private space they have. Some of them will never have met you. They're trusting the WoodBClean name — and that name is built or broken by every person on this team, on every job.

When you are on site: you are WoodBClean. Not just a contractor. Not just a cleaner. You are the face of a business someone chose to trust.

The most important thing Bonnie wants you to know

If there's one quality that separates a WoodBClean cleaner from someone who just wants quick cash, it isn't speed. It isn't even experience. It's common sense.

Common sense in cleaning means: you see something that needs doing, and you do it. Not because it was on a checklist. Because you're a professional who gives a damn about the outcome.

What common sense looks like on the job

1
You're cleaning a door frame on a new build and notice paint overspray on the glass
You don't leave it. You identify the right tool, use the right technique, and remove it. That's what a professional does.
2
You're doing a bond clean and spot a sticker on a window
You remove it. An agent will find it. Don't walk past it because it wasn't mentioned in the brief.
3
You finish cleaning a bathroom and notice the mirror has a smudge from where you leaned near it
You go back and fix it before you leave. Every time. Without being asked.
4
You're cleaning a kitchen and notice the top of the range hood is thick with grease
It wasn't on the job sheet — but you're a professional. You address it, or you flag it to Bonnie if it's beyond the scope of the booking.
5
You finish a job early
You don't sit in your car and wait. You do another pass. You check the rooms again. You look for what you might have missed. Then you leave when the job is genuinely done.

The question to ask yourself before you leave any job

Would I be happy coming home to this?
Stand at the door of each room before you leave. Look at it like a client would. If the answer is anything other than yes — go back and fix what's holding you back.
💡
Common sense is a skill. It doesn't mean doing extra work for free. It means caring enough about the outcome that you don't leave a job half-done. Clients notice. Bonnie notices. And over time, it's what builds a reputation that opens doors.

Written reflections — prove you've thought about this

These aren't quiz questions. There are no right or wrong answers. Write what you actually think — in your own words. This is about showing you've genuinely engaged with what WoodBClean stands for.

1. In your own words — why did Bonnie start WoodBClean, and why does that story matter to how you do your job?
2. You're cleaning a bond property and notice the exhaust fan in the bathroom is thick with dust — it wasn't mentioned in the job brief. What do you do, and why?
3. A client you've cleaned for twice approaches you at the end of a job and says "I'd love to just book you directly — save us both the hassle." What do you say, word for word? And what do you do straight after?
4. What does "common sense" mean to you in the context of cleaning? Give two specific examples of what it looks like in practice on a real job.

Module 2 · Your role & responsibilities

Your role and responsibilities

What your engagement with WoodBClean means in practice — pay, entitlements, obligations, and your rights at work. This week is tailored to your role.

Module 1 recap3 quick questions before Module 2
Module 1 recap — 3 questions

You are a WoodBClean employee

As a WoodBClean employee, you are engaged under an employment agreement. WoodBClean is your employer — you are covered by the Fair Work Act 2009, the National Employment Standards, and Queensland WHS law.

This means WoodBClean has obligations to you — providing PPE, covering you under applicable insurance, and providing a safe work environment. WoodBClean pays your wages and covers you under WorkCover Queensland. As a subcontractor, you invoice WoodBClean for your services at the agreed rate. You have obligations in return — including following our policies, maintaining quality standards, and conducting yourself professionally at all times.

You are a WoodBClean subcontractor

As a WoodBClean subcontractor, you are engaged as an independent contractor — not an employee. You operate your own business, invoice WoodBClean for your services, and are responsible for your own tax, superannuation, and insurance obligations.

WoodBClean has obligations to you — including paying your invoices within agreed terms, providing a safe work environment, supplying cleaning products for WoodBClean jobs, and giving you reasonable notice of job requirements. You have obligations in return — including maintaining your ABN, meeting WoodBClean quality standards, holding required insurance, and following our safety procedures.
General advice only. This information is general in nature only. You should obtain advice from a registered tax agent or financial adviser regarding your individual circumstances.
If you are ever unsure whether your arrangement with WoodBClean is correctly classified as contracting, seek independent advice from the ATO (ato.gov.au) or Fair Work Ombudsman (13 13 94). Both have free guidance on employee vs contractor status.

What applies to both roles

Key takeaway
Whether you are an employee or subcontractor, WoodBClean expects the same standard of work, professionalism, and care. The difference is in how you are paid and what legal protections apply — not in how well you do the job.
Regardless of your engagement type, the following applies to everyone at WoodBClean:

— WoodBClean values and code of conduct
— Key handling and security policies
— Non-solicitation obligations
— All chemical safety, PPE, and SWMS requirements
— Photo documentation and WhatsApp communication policy
— WoodBClean cleaning standards and quality requirements
— Confidentiality of client information
— Privacy Act obligations regarding client data
— Workplace bullying and harassment policy

The standard of your work and your professional conduct are identical whether you are an employee or subcontractor. You represent WoodBClean on every job.

Before reading this section — do you know the difference between a base rate and a penalty rate? What situations do you think might attract a higher rate of pay?

A base rate is your standard hourly pay. Penalty rates are higher rates that apply for evenings, weekends, and public holidays — they exist because working outside normal hours is less desirable and the Fair Work Act protects you from being underpaid for it.
How your wages work

Your specific wage rate is confirmed in your individual employment agreement with Bonnie. This overview explains how the pay structure works so you know what to expect.

Tier 1
New starter

Tier 2

Tier 3

Your entitlements under the National Employment Standards

Annual leave — 4 weeks paid per year
Pro-rata for part-time. Request through Bonnie with reasonable notice.
Personal and carer leave — 10 days paid per year
For illness or caring responsibilities. A medical certificate may be required for absences over 2 consecutive days.
Compassionate leave — 2 days paid per occasion
For the death or serious illness of an immediate family member.
Superannuation — paid at the legislated rate
Paid into your nominated super fund each pay period. Confirm your fund details with Bonnie.
Payslip every pay period
Check it every time. If anything looks wrong — contact Bonnie immediately.
For independent advice on your entitlements: Fair Work Ombudsman at fairwork.gov.au or call 13 13 94.

How payments work — subcontractors

You are paid by invoice. Submit a tax invoice to WoodBClean at the end of each week covering all jobs completed. WoodBClean pays your invoice within the agreed payment terms confirmed in your subcontractor agreement.

Your hourly rate is confirmed in your individual agreement with Bonnie. Full invoicing instructions, ABN requirements, and a worked invoice example are in the Subcontractor portal in the sidebar.

Your financial obligations as a subcontractor

ABN — required before invoicing
Register free at abr.business.gov.au if you do not yet have one. Takes approximately 10 minutes.
Income tax — your responsibility
WoodBClean does not withhold tax from your payments. You must declare all income in your annual tax return. Set aside approximately 25–30% of your earnings for tax.
Superannuation — generally your responsibility
As a contractor you are generally responsible for your own super. Check with an accountant or the ATO regarding your specific situation.
GST — register if turnover exceeds $75,000
If your total annual turnover from all sources reaches $75,000 you must register for GST. Below this threshold registration is optional.

Insurance — required for subcontractors

Public liability insurance — requiredCovers you if a client property is damaged or a third party is injured as a result of your work. Required before commencing any WoodBClean job. WoodBClean can provide guidance on suitable policies — speak with Bonnie.
Income protection insurance — strongly recommendedCovers lost income if you cannot work due to injury or illness. Unlike employees, subcontractors are not automatically covered by WorkCover Queensland. Policies start from approximately $30–60 per month.

Privacy — handling client information

As a WoodBClean team member, you regularly access personal information about clients — their home address, phone number, access codes, and details about their property and personal circumstances. This is protected under the Privacy Act 1988 (Commonwealth).

Privacy rules — always

Use client information only for the job it was given to you forA client address is for getting to the job — nothing else.
Keep all client details strictly confidentialNever share names, addresses, phone numbers, or access codes with anyone outside WoodBClean.
Never photograph anything personal at a client propertyJob documentation photos only. Never photograph personal items, documents, valuables, or private spaces.
Never discuss client details on social media or with outsidersEven saying you cleaned a house in a particular suburb and describing it can breach privacy.
Never use client contact details to solicit workUsing a phone number or address obtained through work to contact a client privately is both a privacy breach and a non-solicitation breach.
If you are ever unsure whether sharing information is appropriate — do not share it. Check with Bonnie first.

Equal opportunity

Under Queensland and Commonwealth anti-discrimination law, everyone has the right to work without being treated less favourably because of a protected attribute. At WoodBClean we are committed to equal opportunity regardless of race, gender, age, disability, religion, or sexual orientation.

Do not make jokes or comments about any of these attributes. Do not treat a colleague or client differently based on who they are.

If you believe you have been treated unfairly, report it to Bonnie. You can also contact the Queensland Human Rights Commission: 1300 130 670.

Right to disconnect — Fair Work Act 2024

💡
Did you know?The Right to Disconnect law (Fair Work Act 2024) means your employer generally cannot expect you to monitor or respond to messages outside your working hours without reasonable compensation. This is a genuine legal right — not just a courtesy.
Under changes to the Fair Work Act effective August 2024, employees have the right to reasonably refuse contact from their employer outside of agreed working hours, unless it is an emergency or unreasonable to do so.

At WoodBClean this means: outside your agreed working hours, you are not obligated to respond to non-urgent messages. Bonnie will always indicate when something is genuinely urgent.

WoodBClean has zero tolerance for workplace bullying

Under the Queensland Work Health and Safety Act 2011 and the Fair Work Act 2009, every person has the right to a workplace free from bullying and harassment — whether you are an employee or a subcontractor, and whether the behaviour comes from a manager, a colleague, or a client.

What counts as bullying

Verbal abuse and humiliationYelling, insulting, or belittling someone — including in front of others or via WhatsApp.
Exclusion or isolationDeliberately leaving someone out of conversations or team communication for non-work reasons.
Spreading rumours or gossipSharing false or private information about a colleague — in person or on social media.
Physical intimidation or aggressionAny threatening behaviour or physical aggression.
Sexual harassmentUnwelcome conduct of a sexual nature — illegal under the Sex Discrimination Act 1984. Zero tolerance.
Reasonable management action — like setting performance expectations or addressing conduct — is not bullying, even if it feels uncomfortable.

What to do if you experience or witness bullying

❌ What not to do
Post about it online, confront the person aggressively, or ignore it hoping it will stop on its own.
✅ What to do
Document what happened with dates and details, speak to Bonnie directly, and if unresolved, contact the Fair Work Commission.
1
If safe to do so — tell the person their behaviour is not acceptable
2
Keep a record — dates, times, what was said or done, who witnessed it
3
Report to Bonnie — all concerns are taken seriously and handled confidentially
4
External support if needed
Fair Work Commission: 1300 799 675 | Australian Human Rights Commission: 1300 656 419
No one at WoodBClean will face negative consequences for genuinely reporting a bullying or harassment concern. Retaliation is itself a serious breach of policy.

Right to refuse unsafe work — employees

Under the Queensland Work Health and Safety Act 2011, you have the legal right to stop work if you believe it presents a serious risk to your health or safety — without facing penalties or dismissal for doing so.

If you are asked to work in a situation you genuinely believe is unsafe: tell Bonnie immediately, describe the hazard, and do not re-enter until it is resolved. You cannot be disciplined for a genuine safety refusal.

Independent advice: WorkSafe Queensland — 1300 362 128.

Workers compensation — employees

As a WoodBClean employee, if you are injured at work you are automatically covered by WorkCover Queensland workers compensation.

Report all injuries to Bonnie the same day. Delayed reporting can affect your claim. Seek medical attention and keep all medical certificates and receipts.

WorkCover Queensland: 1300 362 128 | worksafe.qld.gov.au

Workers compensation covers medical costs, rehabilitation, and lost wages. You cannot be dismissed for making a legitimate claim.

Right to refuse unsafe work — subcontractors

The right to refuse unsafe work under Queensland WHS law applies to subcontractors as well as employees. You have the right to stop work if you genuinely believe it presents a serious safety risk — without penalty.

Tell Bonnie immediately and describe the hazard clearly. Do not re-enter until the hazard is resolved. Contact WorkSafe Queensland on 1300 362 128 for independent advice.

Injury protection — subcontractors

As an independent contractor, you are generally not covered by WorkCover Queensland workers compensation in the same way employees are. If you are injured on a WoodBClean site, you may not have automatic cover for lost income or medical costs.

Public liability insurance is required — covers damage or injury to third parties. Income protection insurance is strongly recommended — covers your lost income if you cannot work.

WoodBClean can provide guidance on suitable policies. Speak with Bonnie before commencing work if you do not yet have cover.

If you are injured on site: report to Bonnie immediately, seek medical attention, and keep all documentation.

Heat stress — working in Queensland

Queensland summers are extreme. Heat stress is a real WHS hazard — particularly in properties without air conditioning or on outdoor jobs.

Signs of heat stress: Excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, nausea. Heat stroke (stopping sweating, confusion) — call 000 immediately.

Drink at least 600ml of water per hour in hot conditions. Take breaks in cool areas. Tell Bonnie if you feel unwell. No job is worth your health.

Tax in Australia — how it works for employees

As a WoodBClean employee, your tax is handled automatically. WoodBClean withholds tax from your wages each pay period and sends it to the ATO on your behalf. This is called PAYG withholding (Pay As You Go). You never have to worry about setting money aside for tax — it is already taken care of.

At the end of the financial year (30 June) you lodge a tax return with the ATO. Depending on your income and deductions, you may receive a refund or owe a small amount. Most employees who work part-year or have work-related expenses receive a refund.
ATO — new to Australia guide myGov — lodge your tax return ATO — working as an employee
Understanding PAYG withholding — ATO Australia
Australian Tax Office · YouTube

What is a TFN declaration?

A Tax File Number (TFN) declaration is a form you complete when you start a new job. It tells WoodBClean your TFN so they can withhold the correct amount of tax from your wages.

Without a TFN declaration, WoodBClean is legally required to withhold tax at the highest rate (47%). With it, you pay only what you actually owe based on your income.

If you do not have a TFN yet — apply free at ato.gov.au. Takes about 10 minutes and is valid for life.
Apply for a TFN — free, takes 10 minutes

Superannuation — your retirement savings

Superannuation (super) is money set aside for your retirement. Your employer — WoodBClean — is legally required to pay super on top of your wages at the legislated rate (currently 11.5%, rising to 12% by 2025).

This money belongs to you. It goes into a super fund account in your name and grows over time. You generally cannot access it until you retire, but it is genuinely valuable — even small amounts compound significantly over a working life.

You choose your own super fund. If you do not choose one, WoodBClean will pay into a default fund on your behalf — but you can change this at any time.
1
Choose a super fund

How to read your payslip

Every pay period WoodBClean will provide a payslip. Here is what each line means:
WoodBClean — Payslip example
Gross earnings (hours × rate)$620.00
PAYG tax withheld−$93.00
Net pay (what you receive)$527.00
Superannuation (paid separately to your fund)$71.30
Gross earnings — your total pay before tax. Hours worked × your hourly rate.
PAYG tax withheld — the tax WoodBClean sends to the ATO on your behalf. Based on your income and TFN declaration.
Net pay — what actually lands in your bank account.
Superannuation — paid on top of your wages directly to your super fund. You do not receive this in your bank — it goes to your retirement savings.
Check your payslip every single pay period. If the hours, rate, or tax withheld look wrong — contact Bonnie immediately. Errors are much easier to fix when caught early.

Managing your tax and money

As a subcontractor, WoodBClean does not withhold tax from your payments. That means you are responsible for setting money aside yourself. Here is how to do it simply:
1
The 25-30% rule
Every time a payment from WoodBClean hits your account, immediately transfer 25-30% into a separate savings account labelled "Tax". Do not touch this money. At tax time it will be there waiting for you.
2
Keep every receipt
Phone bills (work use portion), equipment, cleaning supplies you buy yourself, car expenses, insurance premiums — these are all potential tax deductions. Keep receipts in a folder or use an app like Dext.
3
Lodge your tax return by 31 October each year
Or earlier if you use a registered tax agent (they often get extended deadlines). Your tax agent will calculate what you owe and identify deductions you may have missed.
4
GST — register if your turnover reaches $75,000
Below $75,000 total annual income from all sources, GST registration is optional. Above it — mandatory. A good accountant will tell you when to register.
Real example: You earn $800 in a week. Transfer $200-$240 to your tax savings immediately. The $600 left is yours to spend. At tax time — no surprises.

The subcontractor job flow — from booking to payment

This is what Bonnie needs to be able to see at any point. Clear, accessible, logged. When this flow breaks down — jobs get missed, clients get let down, and payment gets complicated. Own your part of this process.
1
Job confirmed via WhatsApp
Bonnie sends you job details: address, date, time, job type, and any specific requirements. Reply to confirm within 2 hours. If you don't confirm, Bonnie cannot assume you've seen it.
2
Log the job in your records immediately
Date, address, job type, agreed rate. This is YOUR business — you need your own record of every job you take. A simple notes app, spreadsheet, or diary works fine. Don't rely on WhatsApp history alone — it can be lost.
3
Message Bonnie on arrival
"On site at [address], starting now." This is your official start time. No message = no verified start time = potential payment dispute. Every job. Every time.
4
Take before photos
Photograph the key areas before you start. This protects you if a client later claims damage or incomplete work. It's not about distrust — it's about having a clean record on both sides.
5
Complete the job to WoodBClean standard
Not your standard. WoodBClean standard. You are representing the business. Use the checklists in each module. Do not leave until the job is genuinely done.
6
Take completion photos and message Bonnie
"Job complete at [address]." Send key photos — oven, bathroom, floors, any area that was notably dirty. This is your proof of work and Bonnie's quality check.
7
Submit your tax invoice by end of week
Your invoice must cover every job that week: address, date, hours, rate, total. Email to woodbclean@gmail.com. No invoice = no payment. It's that simple.
8
Payment received within agreed terms
If payment hasn't arrived by the agreed date — contact Bonnie directly. Do not let it sit for weeks. You are running a business. Your cash flow matters.

The WoodBClean job tier system

For larger or more complex jobs, Bonnie specifies which tier of subcontractor she needs. This isn't about ranking people — it's about matching the right person to the right job. Be honest about which tier you are. Taking a Tier 3 job when you're a Tier 1 operator doesn't end well for anyone.
T1
Tier 1 — No experience, no equipment
You are learning. You can assist on jobs under supervision. You use WoodBClean's equipment and follow direction from a lead cleaner. Rate reflects the learning component. Be upfront about where you are — this is a valid starting point.
T2
Tier 2 — Experience, no equipment
You can clean to WoodBClean standard independently but don't yet have your own full equipment kit. WoodBClean may supply equipment. You are responsible for the quality of your work without supervision.
T3
Tier 3 — Experience and equipment
You arrive fully self-sufficient. Your own vacuum, caddy, full Clean Like A Pro product range, and the skills to execute any standard WoodBClean job type independently. This tier attracts the highest rate and the most job opportunities.

Moving between tiers

Tiers are not permanent. As you build your skills and invest in your equipment, you progress. Talk to Bonnie when you believe you've moved up — she'll confirm based on the quality she's seen from you.

The fastest way to move from Tier 1 to Tier 3 is: complete all 16 training modules, shadow experienced cleaners, invest in your own equipment, and demonstrate consistent quality across your first jobs.

Why being honest about your tier matters

Taking a Tier 3 job as a Tier 1 operator means the client gets a substandard result, Bonnie gets a complaint, and you may not get paid for a job the client rejects.
Claiming equipment you don't have creates a situation on site that's impossible to recover from professionally.
Saying "I'm Tier 1 right now but working toward Tier 3" is exactly the kind of honesty that builds a long working relationship with WoodBClean.

Our team is genuinely diverse — and that's a strength

WoodBClean's team comes from many different backgrounds, cultures, and belief systems. This portal is available in 23 languages for a reason. Bonnie is actively mindful of her team's individual circumstances — and she expects the same awareness from everyone on the team toward each other.

This isn't a policy section. It's about being a decent human being in a professional environment.

Religious observance and job allocation

Bonnie makes active decisions about job allocation based on her team's individual circumstances. One real example from WoodBClean's experience:
A team member observing Ramadan — fasting from food and water for 16+ hours during Queensland's summer heat — would not be allocated a full-day new build in direct sun. That's not discrimination. That's Bonnie understanding that putting someone in that situation is a health risk and sets them up to fail. The right job at the right time protects everyone.
If your religious observance, cultural practice, or personal circumstances affect your availability or capacity for certain jobs — tell Bonnie. This information will never be used against you. It will be used to make sure you're set up to succeed.

How this shows up on the job

✓
Respect how your teammates observe their beliefs
Someone may need a moment to pray during a job. Someone may not eat certain foods. Someone may need to step away briefly at specific times. These are normal parts of working in a diverse team — accommodate them with the same professionalism you'd want for yourself.
✓
Never comment on or question a colleague's beliefs
Not your business. Not your call. If something creates a genuine operational issue, raise it with Bonnie — not directly with the person.
✓
Client households are also diverse
You may enter homes with religious symbols, cultural artefacts, or practices very different from your own. Treat every space with the same care and respect, regardless of your personal beliefs.
✓
Language differences on a team job
If you're working with someone who has limited English — be patient, use clear demonstrations, and never make someone feel embarrassed. The work itself communicates quality.
💡
Under the Fair Work Act and Queensland Anti-Discrimination Act, every team member has the right to be free from discrimination based on religion, cultural background, race, gender, age, and more. These aren't just rules — they're the minimum standard. WoodBClean aims higher than the minimum.

What is a Safety Data Sheet?

A Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is a legal document that comes with every hazardous chemical product. It contains everything you need to know about that product — what is in it, the hazards it carries, how to use it safely, what PPE to wear, and what to do if something goes wrong.

Under Queensland WHS law, you have the right to access the SDS for every product you use, and the responsibility to read it before using a product for the first time.

The 4 SDS sections you must read first

1
Watch: Safety Data Sheets — all 16 sections explained
~8 min · Ally Safety
Covers all 16 SDS sections with real product examples. Reading an SDS is a legal requirement under Australian WHS law before handling any chemical.
Section 1 — Identification
Product name, supplier, emergency contact. Save the emergency number.
2
Section 2 — Hazard identification
What hazards does this product carry? What warning symbols apply? Read this first.
4
Section 4 — First aid measures
What to do for skin contact, eye contact, ingestion, inhalation — specific to this product.
8
Section 8 — Exposure controls and PPE
Exactly what gloves, eye protection, or respiratory protection this product requires.
All 16 sections matter, but 1, 2, 4, and 8 are the ones you need before picking up any product for the first time.

Spray bottle labelling — non-negotiable rules

Every bottle must be labelled with the product nameNo label — do not use it. Refill and relabel.
Include dilution rate if it is a diluted productSo anyone picking it up knows exactly what is in it at what strength.
Never put a different product in a bottle without relabellingAn unlabelled or mislabelled bottle is a serious safety hazard and is illegal under WHS regulations.
Never mix two products in the same spray bottleEven if they seem compatible — this is how chemical accidents happen.
Mixing the wrong chemicals can produce toxic gases that cause serious injury or death. This is not an exaggeration. These combinations are never acceptable under any circumstances.

Chemical combinations you must NEVER create

Bleach + ammonia = chloramine gasSeverely damages the respiratory system. Bleach and many glass cleaners, floor cleaners, and bathroom sprays contain ammonia. Always check before combining anything with bleach.
Bleach + vinegar or acidic cleaners = chlorine gasHighly toxic. Never mix bleach with any acidic product.
Different drain cleanersMost contain strong acids or bases. Combining them causes violent reactions, splattering, and toxic fumes.
Any two products not designed to be mixedIf it is not on the label — do not mix it. When in doubt, ask Bonnie.
The Clean Like A Pro product range is designed to be used one product at a time, for its designated purpose. Never combine any two products. Each has its own specific use and they are not designed to work together.

Chemical accident or spill — 5 steps immediately

1
Remove the person from the area — get to fresh air
Do not let them stay in contact with the chemical.
2
Check the SDS — follow the first aid instructions for that specific product
Flush with water, remove contaminated clothing, or other specific actions — the SDS tells you exactly.
3
Call 000 if serious
Swallowed a chemical, trouble breathing, chemical burns — call 000 immediately.
4
Call Poisons Information Centre if unsure — 13 11 26
Available 24 hours, 7 days. Save this number in your phone right now.
5
Report to Bonnie immediately — same day incident report
Every chemical incident — no matter how minor — must be reported and documented.
Poisons Info — 13 11 26 poisonsinfo.org.au

Surface compatibility — which product on which surface

Using the wrong product on the wrong surface causes permanent damage. When in doubt — water and microfibre first. Always test in a hidden area.
Natural stone, marble, and travertine are acid-sensitive. Never use anything with vinegar, citric acid, or bleach on these surfaces. Even one application can etch permanently.

Timber / floating floors⚠️ diluted❌❌❌❌

The #1 chemical mistake at WoodBClean — and how to never make it

The most common mistake Bonnie sees is cleaners not diluting correctly. Not because the instructions aren't there — but because they guess instead of measure. Guessing costs money and damages surfaces.

Clean Like A Pro concentrates come in 5L bottles with a Pro Smooth Flow Cap Tap — a measured-pour dispenser that fits directly onto the 5L bottle. It removes the guesswork entirely. Use it. Every time.

How dilution ratios actually work

A dilution ratio tells you how many parts water to add for every 1 part product. Here's how to read it:
1:10
1 part product
10 parts water
500ml bottle → 45ml product + 455ml water
1:20
1 part product
20 parts water
500ml bottle → 24ml product + 476ml water
Too concentrated — wastes product, leaves residue on surfaces, can damage finishes, and costs more per job than necessary.
Too diluted — product won't do its job. You'll scrub harder, take longer, and the client's home won't actually be clean.
Correct dilution — the product works as designed, your cloths stay cleaner longer, and the job gets done faster. Follow the label. Every time.

Always check the label for the current ratio — these are guides. For precise ratios, refer to the CLAP product guide.

Unlabelled bottle — do not use, do not take to a job

Surfaces and items that must never have product applied

Two categories of things that are off-limits for chemical application at WoodBClean — no matter how dirty they are, no matter how tempting it is to try a product. Damage here means a complaint, a claim, and a damaged relationship with the client.
!
Personal items — never touch, never spray
Clothing, jewellery, makeup, skincare products, medications, personal documents, kids' toys, pet items, wallets, phones, laptops, bags. You are there to clean the space — not to handle or clean personal belongings. If a personal item is in your way, move it carefully by hand to clean underneath, then replace it exactly where it was.
!
Curtains and soft furnishings — never spray directly
Curtains, blinds, fabric lampshades, cushions, throws. Cleaning products — even organic ones — can permanently stain, shrink, or alter the texture of fabric. If curtains need to be moved to clean a window sill, handle them gently. Never spray product near them. A dry microfibre cloth only for dusting.

Other surfaces that need specific care

Natural stone benchtops (marble, granite, travertine) — acid-based products etch stone permanently. PRO Shower is acid-based. Never use it on stone. PRO Harmony (pH neutral) or water only on natural stone surfaces.
Timber floors and furniture — never wet mop, never apply product neat. Damp microfibre cloth only for timber surfaces. Excess moisture causes warping, swelling, and de-lamination that cannot be undone.
Painted walls — test in a hidden spot first. Some paints are water-sensitive. Use PRO Harmony diluted, light pressure, damp cloth. Never scrub painted surfaces.
Gold or brass tapware — acid products remove the finish. Water and microfibre only. PRO Multi-Purpose for polish if needed — no acidic products.
When unsure about any surface — water and microfibre first. Call Bonnie. Never experiment with a client's expensive surfaces.
💡
The golden rule: If you wouldn't be confident explaining what you did to Bonnie and the client straight after — don't do it. Common sense applies to chemicals the same way it applies to everything else at WoodBClean.

PPE, SWMS and incident reporting

Your legal obligations around personal protective equipment, safe work method statements, and how to handle incidents correctly when they occur.

Module 3 recap3 quick questions before Module 4
Module 3 recap — 3 questions

PPE — your first line of defence

PPE is not optional. It is both a legal requirement under Queensland WHS law and a condition of your engagement with WoodBClean. The specific PPE required for each task is in the SDS for that product and our SWMS documents.
Employees: WoodBClean provides all standard PPE — gloves, safety glasses, and non-slip footwear. Bonnie will confirm where to collect your PPE before your first job — this may be on site, in your assigned vehicle, or handed to you directly. Replace worn or damaged PPE through Bonnie.
Subcontractors: You are responsible for providing your own standard PPE meeting WoodBClean requirements. Contact Bonnie for guidance on suitable products. For specialist jobs WoodBClean will confirm any additional requirements in advance.

PPE rules — standard for every job

Gloves — all bathroom work, no exceptionsBathrooms contain biological contamination regardless of how clean they look. Gloves on for the entire time you are working in any bathroom — whether scrubbing a toilet or simply wiping a tap.
Gloves — all chemical product use throughout the propertyAny time you are applying a cleaning product anywhere — gloves on.
Safety glasses — all spray product useAny time you are spraying a product there is a risk of splash to the eyes. Mandatory.
Non-slip, closed-toe footwear — every jobSlip hazards from wet floors are the most common cause of cleaning industry injuries.
Clean, presentable uniformPresentation and a basic layer of protection. Always worn on site.
When gloves are not mandatoryDry tasks with no chemical or biological contact — making beds with fresh linen, restocking sealed supplies, emptying bin liners. Use your judgement. When in doubt, wear them.

Specialist PPE for specific tasks

P2
P2 dust mask — new builds and active construction sites
Mandatory when construction dust is actively airborne. P2-rated only — surgical masks do not filter silica particles. Put it on as soon as you begin disturbing settled dust during cleaning.
L1
P2 respirator, goggles, disposable gloves — Level 1 mould treatment
Standard gloves and glasses are not enough for mould work. Full procedure in the Mould module.
L2
Full Tyvek suit, P3 respirator — Level 2 mould remediation only
Approved staff only. Covered in the locked Level 2 mould module.
Safe Work Australia — PPE guide WorkSafe Queensland

What is a SWMS?

A Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) is a written document that identifies the high-risk work involved in a task, describes how risks will be controlled, and must be read and signed by workers before the task begins.

At WoodBClean, SWMS are required for high-risk tasks. Your signature on a SWMS is a legal declaration that you have read it, understood it, and will follow it.

When you need a SWMS at WoodBClean

New build and post-construction cleansConstruction sites are high-risk work environments. SWMS required before starting any new build clean.
Level 2 mould remediationWhole-home remediation is classified as hazardous work. SWMS must be signed before entering the site.
Working at height above 2 metresLadders or scaffolding above 2 metres require a SWMS risk assessment.
Any task Bonnie identifies as high-riskIf Bonnie provides a SWMS for a task — read it and sign it before starting.

Your SWMS obligations

1
Read it completely before signing
You are signing to say you have read, understood, and will follow it. That is a legal document. Do not skim and sign.
2
Ask questions if anything is unclear
Ask Bonnie before you sign — never sign a SWMS if you do not fully understand it.
3
Follow it exactly during the task
Deviating from a signed SWMS defeats its entire purpose and removes your legal protection.
4
Never start a SWMS-required task without signing first
This is a legal requirement. There are no exceptions.

Why incident reporting matters

Incident reporting is a legal requirement under Queensland WHS law. Every incident, near miss, or hazard that is reported gives WoodBClean the information needed to prevent it happening again. Reporting is not about blame — it is about improvement. You will never be punished for reporting an incident honestly.

What must be reported

Any injury to yourself or another personCuts, slips, chemical exposure, muscle strains — any physical injury however minor.
Near missesSomething that almost caused an injury but did not. These are early warnings that prevent future incidents.
Property damageAny damage to a client property — no matter how minor. Report immediately before leaving.
Chemical spills or exposuresAny spill of a cleaning product — in a vehicle or on site.
Lost or misplaced keysAll key incidents must be reported the same day.

How to report

1
Call Bonnie immediately — same day for all incidents
For serious incidents — call straight away, even mid-job.
2
Complete a written incident report form
Your manager will provide the form. Include: what happened, where, when, who was involved, and what was done immediately.
3
For injuries requiring medical attention — 000 first
Safety first. Everything else can wait.
Covering up an incident — even a small one — is always worse than reporting it. If something goes wrong and it later comes out that you knew and did not report, the consequences are far more serious than the original incident.

A real incident at WoodBClean — chemical inhalation

This happened. Bonnie is sharing it so it never happens to you.
What happened
A cleaner used bleach in an unventilated bathroom. The space was small, the door was closed, and they were working quickly. Within minutes they had breathed in a significant amount of chemical fumes — dizziness, burning throat, watering eyes.
Why bleach is not in the WoodBClean kit: This is one of the reasons WoodBClean uses the Clean Like A Pro range exclusively. Bleach produces chlorine gas fumes — especially in warm, enclosed spaces like bathrooms. Even short-term inhalation causes respiratory irritation. Repeated exposure causes lasting lung damage.

What should have happened: Window open. Door open. P2 mask if using any strong chemical in an enclosed space. And ideally — not using bleach at all, which is why WoodBClean doesn't.
If you ever feel dizzy, nauseous, or have a burning throat while working — stop immediately, leave the space, get fresh air, and call Bonnie. Do not push through it. Chemical inhalation symptoms can escalate quickly in enclosed spaces.

Manual handling — protecting your body

Back strains, shoulder injuries, and wrist problems are the most common injuries in the cleaning industry. Most are preventable. Using a backpack vacuum instead of an upright is one example of WoodBClean actively reducing your manual handling risk.

Safe lifting — every time

1
Plan before you lift — check weight, clear path, know where it is going
2
Stand close, feet shoulder-width apart, stable footing
3
Bend your knees — never your back — keep your spine upright
4
Grip firmly, hold load close to your body, lift by straightening your legs
5
Turn your feet to change direction — never twist your spine while carrying
6
Ask for help or use equipment for anything too heavy to lift safely alone

Repetitive strain injury prevention

Cleaning involves many repetitive movements. RSI affecting wrists, shoulders, and elbows is common over time.

Switch hands periodically when wiping large surfaces. Do not grip spray bottles too tightly. Stretch hands, wrists, and shoulders during breaks. Report any persistent aching or pain to Bonnie early — do not wait until it becomes a serious injury.
Safe manual handling techniques — WorkSafe
WorkSafe Queensland · YouTube

Heat stress — Queensland is serious

🌡
Signs of heat stress
Excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, nausea, weakness. If you notice these — stop work, move to shade or a cool area, drink water, tell Bonnie.
!
Heat stroke — call 000 immediately
Stopping sweating, confusion, hot dry skin, loss of consciousness. This is a medical emergency.
💧
Prevention
Drink at least 600ml of water per hour in hot conditions. Take rest breaks in cool areas. Never push through heat exhaustion to finish a job. No deadline is worth a medical emergency.

Fatigue management

Fatigue affects judgement, reaction times, and the quality of your work — and it affects your safety on the road. If you are too tired to work or drive safely, contact Bonnie before the job. No job is worth an accident.

If you feel drowsy while driving — pull over at the next safe location, take a 15-minute rest, and call Bonnie.

The two most common safety failures at WoodBClean

Bonnie has seen a lot of things on jobs. The two that worry her most aren't dramatic accidents — they're the small, daily choices that people make because they don't think it'll matter. No gloves. Wrong shoes. These two things alone are responsible for the majority of preventable injuries in the cleaning industry.

Gloves — the non-negotiable

There is no job at WoodBClean where bare hands are acceptable when using chemicals or working in bathrooms. None. Here's why this matters more than it might seem:
!
Skin absorption is real and cumulative
Cleaning chemicals absorb through skin — especially between fingers, over knuckles, and under rings. One job without gloves won't kill you. Two hundred jobs without gloves and your skin barrier is damaged, your body has absorbed trace chemicals daily, and you are at real risk of occupational dermatitis and chemical sensitivity that can end your cleaning career.
!
Bathrooms contain biological contamination — always
Even a bathroom that looks spotless contains bacteria and biological material invisible to the eye. Gloves on for the entire bathroom — not just the toilet. Tap handles, shower doors, vanity surfaces — all of it.
!
A cut or break in the skin changes everything
Any small cut, hangnail, or cracked skin on your bare hand becomes a direct entry point for chemicals and bacteria. If you have any broken skin on your hands — gloves are even more critical, not less.
If Bonnie sees you without gloves in a bathroom or while using product — it is an immediate conversation. This isn't about being strict. It's about the fact that she has seen what repeated chemical exposure without protection does to people over time.

Footwear — the other one that matters

The cleaning industry has one of the highest rates of slips, trips, and falls of any occupation in Australia. Wet floors, wet tiles, wet bathrooms — every job has slippery surfaces. What you have on your feet determines whether a wet floor is a hazard or just a wet floor.
Non-slip, closed-toe shoes — rubber sole with grip pattern. If you can feel the floor through the sole, they're not adequate for a cleaning job.
Comfortable and supportive — you are on your feet for hours. Back pain and knee issues from poor footwear are cumulative and career-ending over time.
Thongs, sandals, or open-toed shoes — never on any WoodBClean job. Chemical spills, dropped equipment, and wet floors make these a serious injury risk.
Fashion sneakers with smooth soles — no grip, no protection. Not suitable for wet environments.
Worn-out shoes with degraded grip — check your soles regularly. Replace when grip is worn smooth.
💡
On new build sites: closed-toe shoes with a solid sole are mandatory. Steel-capped boots are strongly recommended — you are walking through active construction areas where dropped tools, nails, and sharp debris are on the floor.

New build sites are different — treat them differently

A residential home is a controlled, private environment. A new build or construction site is an active worksite with different rules, different hazards, and different legal obligations. Before you step foot on any new build site for the first time, this is what Bonnie walks you through — and what you need to know before she does.

Bonnie's 4-step new build briefing

1
Walk through the jobsite before you touch anything
Don't start cleaning immediately. Walk through with Bonnie or the builder's site supervisor. Identify hazards — unfinished edges, open holes, electrical work, wet concrete, unstable surfaces. Know the site before you work it.
2
Gloves on from the moment you arrive
Construction sites have chemical residue, sharp materials, and biological hazards from site workers. Gloves go on in the car park. Not when you get to the bathroom — before you even pick anything up.
3
Check your shoes
Closed-toe, non-slip, solid sole. New builds have nails, screws, broken tiles, and sharp debris on floors throughout. Thongs or flimsy footwear on a construction site is a serious injury waiting to happen. Steel-capped boots preferred.
4
Be observant — you are on someone else's worksite
Builders, trades, and inspectors may still be on site while you clean. Respect the site rules. Don't go into areas you haven't been cleared for. If a trade tells you to hold off in a particular area — hold off and tell Bonnie. Never argue with site personnel. You are a visitor on their worksite.

Silica dust — the invisible hazard on new builds

Silica dust is produced when concrete, plaster, and tile are cut, drilled, or sanded on construction sites. Silicosis is an incurable lung disease caused by breathing silica dust — and it can develop from relatively short-term exposure at high concentrations.

On active new build sites where cutting or sanding is still happening: P2 mask — mandatory. A surgical mask does not filter silica particles. P2-rated only.
P2 dust mask — wear whenever dust is actively airborne or disturbed during cleaning
Wet-wipe dusty surfaces before sweeping — this suppresses silica particles rather than launching them into the air
Dry sweeping or blowing dust on a new build — this makes silica airborne and puts you and everyone on site at risk
If a site supervisor or builder gives you a safety instruction you don't understand — stop, ask Bonnie before proceeding. You have the right to a safe work environment. You also have the responsibility to follow site rules. Both are true at the same time.

Why this matters — in your own words

Understanding the why behind safety rules is what separates someone who follows them when watched versus someone who follows them because they genuinely get it. This is your chance to prove you understand.

Task 1 — Hydration on the job

Professional cleaning in Australian conditions is physical work. You are moving constantly, often in warm spaces, carrying equipment. Dehydration doesn't announce itself — it creeps up. By the time you feel thirsty, you are already behind.

Module 4 recap — 3 questions

What you need to turn up with

The kit question at WoodBClean depends entirely on your role. Employees working on contracted sites will find everything they need already there. For subcontractors — your kit is your business. Turning up without the right equipment means the job doesn't get done to standard, and that reflects on WoodBClean.

Employees — what WoodBClean provides

WoodBClean employees are engaged for contracted site work. All equipment and chemicals are provided at the site — you will not need to supply your own. Bonnie will confirm exactly what's available before your first shift at any site. If anything is missing or faulty, report it to Bonnie immediately — never improvise with unsuitable equipment.

Subcontractors — your minimum kit

This is what Bonnie expects a Tier 2 or Tier 3 subcontractor to own and arrive with. Your kit is your livelihood — invest in it properly.
1
Vacuum — backpack preferred
A backpack vacuum is strongly preferred at WoodBClean. It distributes weight across your spine, reduces back strain on long jobs, and gives you far better reach for ceilings, fans, and stairs. An upright vacuum is acceptable for Tier 2 while you build toward a backpack. Whatever you have — it must have working suction and a clean filter before every job.
2
Mop and bucket
A flat microfibre mop is the professional standard — it picks up more, uses less water, and is gentler on floors. A string mop is acceptable but check the head is clean before every job. Your bucket must be clean. Arriving with a dirty bucket tells Bonnie everything about your standards.
3
Colour-coded microfibre cloths
Minimum: red for bathrooms, green for kitchen, blue for general surfaces. At least 3 of each per job — you should never run out mid-job. Edgeless microfibre cloths from Clean Like A Pro are recommended. Wash after every job — never arrive with used cloths.
4
Clean Like A Pro product range
Bonnie provides the CLAP Starter Pack to get you started. After that, product arrangements are negotiated directly with Bonnie based on job volume and type. You must always have the full range available — turning up without your mould product on a mould job is not acceptable.
5
PRO360 spray bottles — labelled
At least 4 labelled spray bottles — one per product type (shower, degreaser, multi-purpose, harmony). Labels written clearly with product name and dilution ratio. Filled correctly before the job, not at the client's sink.
6
Caddy or PRO Utility
Your products and tools need to travel with you room to room without trips back to the car. A caddy or the Clean Like A Pro PRO Utility bucket caddy keeps everything accessible. Digging through a bag on every room is slow and unprofessional.
7
PPE — always
Gloves (multiple pairs per job), safety glasses, non-slip closed-toe footwear. P2 mask if going to a new build. This is your responsibility as a subcontractor.
Before your first WoodBClean job — message Bonnie to confirm your kit is complete. She would rather know in advance than find out on site that something's missing.
Employees: All equipment including backpack vacuums is provided by WoodBClean. Bonnie will confirm where to collect equipment before your first job — this may be on site, in your assigned vehicle, or handed to you directly. Report faults to Bonnie immediately.
Subcontractors: WoodBClean supplies cleaning products for WoodBClean jobs. Equipment arrangements will be confirmed with Bonnie — generally WoodBClean equipment is available for use on WoodBClean sites.

Why WoodBClean uses backpack vacuums

WHS rationale: Traditional upright vacuums require constant bending, pushing and pulling that causes back injuries over time. Backpack vacuums distribute weight evenly across the spine and allow natural movement — this is a deliberate WHS decision, not a preference.

Better clean: You can vacuum ceiling fans, walls, vents, and hard-to-reach areas far more easily. Better mobility around furniture and up stairs. Faster on large jobs.

Backpack vacuum — correct use every time

1
Check the filter before every use
A clogged filter reduces suction, overheats the motor, and blows dust back into the air. Tap or wash the filter if it is dirty. Never use with a blocked filter.
2
Check the bag or canister — empty when two-thirds full
A full bag dramatically reduces suction and makes the motor work harder.
3
Fit it correctly — shoulder straps adjusted so unit sits against your back
A poorly fitted backpack vacuum causes the same strain it is designed to prevent.
4
Use the correct attachment for each surface
Floor brush for hard floors and carpet. Crevice tool for skirting boards and tracks. Brush attachment for ceiling fans, vents, and fly screens.
5
Always work top to bottom — ceiling fans first, floors last
Dust falls downward. Vacuuming floors before fans means doing them twice.
6
Never vacuum wet or liquid debris
Backpack vacuums are dry only. Vacuuming liquid destroys the motor. If there is liquid — mop first.
7
Store correctly after use — upright, filter cleaned, bag checked

Mops and buckets

Change mop water after every room — without exceptionDirty mop water spreads bacteria and grime from one room to the next. This is one of the most commonly overlooked standards in cleaning — do not let it be yours.
Start every job with clean, fresh clothsUsed cloths from a previous job must never go into a new client home.
Microfibre cloths — the right moisture levelToo wet = leaves streaks. Too dry = does not pick up product residue. Damp is correct for most surfaces. Barely damp or dry for the final pass on glass and mirrors.

Squeegees for glass and shower screens

1
Apply Pro Multi-Purpose evenly across the entire surface
2
Squeegee in smooth overlapping strokes — top to bottom
Wipe the squeegee blade clean between each stroke.
3
Final wipe with a dry edgeless cloth — check from an angle
Streaks are easiest to spot when light hits the glass at an angle.

Pro Utility tool — tracks, grout and detail work

Use for window tracks (spray product, agitate with tool, wipe out debris), grout lines with mould or soap scum, and anywhere a cloth cannot reach — around taps, behind fixtures, along sill edges.

The colour coding system

Colour coding prevents cross-contamination between areas. Using a bathroom cloth on a kitchen surface is a hygiene and food safety risk. The system is simple and non-negotiable.
RED
Bathrooms and toilets only
Never used anywhere else in the property under any circumstances.
GREEN
Kitchen surfaces
Benchtops, appliances, kitchen areas only.
BLUE
General surfaces
Furniture, walls, general areas throughout the property.
YELLOW
Floors and low-risk areas
Confirm the specific colour system for your kit with Bonnie.
A red cloth used outside a bathroom is a serious hygiene failure. If you accidentally use the wrong colour cloth — remove it from service immediately and start again with the correct colour.
More product is not better. Exceeding the recommended dilution rate can damage surfaces, leave residue, create safety hazards, and waste product. Always follow the label.

Dilution guidance — Clean Like A Pro range

PS
Pro Shower — check label for your specific variant
Some are ready to use, some are concentrates. Never guess — check the label.
PB
Pro Bathroom and Toilet — ready to use
Apply directly. Do not dilute.
PD
Pro Degreaser — dilute as per label, stronger for heavy oven grease
For bench tops: dilute as directed. For oven interiors with heavy baked-on grease: stronger rate per SDS. Never exceed SDS instructions.
PM
Pro Multi-Purpose — ready to use
Apply directly. Light spray only — over-application causes streaks.
PH
Pro Harmony — dilute as directed for surfaces and mopping
For floor mopping: follow label ratio per litre. For surfaces: correct dilution in spray bottle.
PMo
Pro Mould — NEVER dilute. Ready to use only.
Diluting reduces effectiveness. Used at full concentration only.

When equipment is not working

1
Stop using the equipment immediately
Never continue using equipment that is clearly not functioning correctly.
2
Check for simple causes first
Vacuum: is the filter clogged? Is the bag full? Is a hose blocked? Many faults are simple maintenance issues.
3
Report to Bonnie if you cannot resolve it
Do not try to fix electrical equipment yourself.
4
Tag faulty equipment clearly — DO NOT USE — FAULT REPORTED [date]
Never put faulty equipment back into general use without it being checked.

Mopping — the technique most cleaners get wrong

Mopping looks simple. It isn't. Done wrong, you're not cleaning the floor — you're spreading dirty water around it. The difference between a clean floor and a smeared floor comes down to three things: water temperature, water change frequency, and technique.

Correct mop technique — step by step

1
Start with hot, clean water and correct product dilution
Hot water lifts grease and grime far more effectively than cold. Add your PRO Harmony at the correct dilution — not more. More product does not mean cleaner floors. It means residue buildup that attracts dirt faster.
2
Change your water after every room — without exception
This is the rule Bonnie repeats most. Grey mop water does not clean. It deposits bacteria and grime from the last room onto the next. If you only remember one thing from this tab — it's this. Every room = fresh water.
3
Figure-8 technique on the floor
Figure-8 strokes — overlapping S-curves — keep the mop head picking up debris rather than pushing it. Straight back-and-forth pushes dirt to the edges and leaves lines. Figure-8 covers every centimetre and keeps the mop engaged with the floor properly.
4
Work back toward the exit — never mop yourself into a corner
Start at the furthest point from the door. Work backwards toward the exit so you never step on clean floor. Walking across a freshly mopped floor defeats the entire purpose.
5
Damp mop only on timber and laminate — never wet
Timber and laminate floors warp, swell, and delaminate when over-wet. Wring your mop until it is barely damp for these surfaces. If the floor looks wet after you mop it — that's too much water. Always.
6
Let the floor dry before replacing mats or furniture
A wet mat on a timber floor traps moisture underneath — exactly what causes the warping you're trying to avoid. Wait until the floor is genuinely dry before putting anything back.

Mop head care

Rinse mop head thoroughly after every job — wring out, hang to dry, never leave it wet in a bucket
Machine wash microfibre mop heads weekly — hot wash, no fabric softener
Arriving at a job with a mop head that smells — this means bacterial growth. Replace it before the job, not after the client complains.
Storing a wet mop head in a sealed bag in your car — bacterial and mould growth guaranteed within hours in Queensland heat

Why microfibre actually works — and why it stops working

Microfibre isn't just a marketing term. There's real science behind why it cleans better than cotton — and real consequences to using it incorrectly.

The science in plain language

A microfibre cloth is made of fibres 1/100th the diameter of a human hair. Because of their microscopic size, the fibres create an enormous surface area with tiny wedge-shaped gaps between them. These gaps act like hooks that:
1
Physically trap bacteria and particles rather than pushing them around
A clean, damp microfibre cloth can remove up to 99% of bacteria from a surface using only water — no chemical needed. This is why colour coding matters so much — if the cloth is carrying bacteria from a bathroom, it will deposit them on whatever you wipe next.
2
Hold onto dirt until you rinse — not release it mid-clean
Unlike cotton, microfibre holds captured particles in the weave until you wash it out. This means a single cloth can do more surface area before it's saturated — as long as you use it correctly.
3
Work with less product, less water, less effort
Microfibre's effectiveness means you need less chemical to achieve the same result. This is why over-spraying product with microfibre creates problems — the cloth absorbs the excess and smears it rather than wiping it.

How to wash microfibre correctly — this is where most people go wrong

Hot wash — 60°C minimum to kill bacteria and reset the fibres
Wash separately from other laundry — microfibre picks up lint from cotton items and clogs the fibres permanently
Mild detergent only — small amount, fully dissolved before adding cloths
No fabric softener — ever. Fabric softener coats the microfibre fibres with a waxy film that fills the wedge-shaped gaps. Once this happens, the cloth can no longer trap bacteria or absorb product. It just pushes things around. A microfibre cloth washed with fabric softener is worse than useless — it looks clean and isn't doing its job.
No tumble dryer on high heat — melts synthetic fibres, destroys the structure. Air dry or low heat only.

When to replace a microfibre cloth

Microfibre cloths don't last forever. Replace when you notice: pilling on the surface, reduced absorbency (water beads rather than absorbs), persistent odour even after a hot wash, or visible damage to the weave. A worn-out microfibre cloth is not doing what you think it's doing.

Module 6 · Core cleaning principles

Core cleaning principles

The universal rules that apply to every WoodBClean job regardless of clean type. Master these and everything else becomes easier.

Module 5 recap3 quick questions before Module 6
Module 5 recap — 3 questions

The 5 rules that apply to every single WoodBClean job

1
Watch: Correct mopping technique — professional cleaning training
~3 min · Servicon
Safe bucket setup, correct mopping technique, water change frequency, and slip hazard prevention. Fully WHS compliant professional cleaning training.
Photograph pre-existing damage on arrival — before touching anything
Walk the entire property with your phone on arrival. Photograph every mark, stain, hole, chip, or broken item before you start cleaning. Send to Bonnie immediately. This is your legal protection — and the client protection — if any dispute arises later about damage.
2
Vacuum first — always, before any wet cleaning
Before any product is applied or any wet cloth touches a surface, the entire property must be vacuumed. Vacuuming after wet cleaning spreads wet debris and undoes your work. Vacuum first. Every time. No exceptions.
3
Top to bottom, back to front — in every room
Top to bottom: Ceiling fans and cornices first. Walls and surfaces next. Skirting boards. Floors last. Gravity means debris falls down — if you clean floors first you will be redoing them.

Back to front: Start at the back of each room and work toward the door. This means you never walk on freshly mopped floors or re-contaminate areas you have already cleaned.
4
Door shut = room complete
The door-shut system originated from new build cleans — where keeping finished rooms sealed prevents construction dust from drifting back in. We apply it to every WoodBClean clean. When a room meets our standard — door closed. Open door = work in progress. Closed door = done. Do not re-enter a closed room unless absolutely necessary.
5
Comprehensive photos before leaving — sent to Bonnie via WhatsApp
Every completed room, every key area. Before you leave any job — not from your car, not from home — photos are sent via WhatsApp. The timestamp is your official completion record. These photos are your protection if any dispute arises.

What to photograph — and when

On arrival — pre-existing damage
Every mark, stain, hole, or damaged item before you touch anything. Send to Bonnie immediately via WhatsApp.
Each completed room — wide shot from doorway
One photo showing the full completed state of the room.
Oven interior and door glass — close-up
Spotless door glass is the most commonly inspected item by agents.
Shower screen and shower floor
Streak-free screen, clean tiles. Zoom in on grout lines if previously mouldy.
Windows — glass, tracks, and sills
Streak-free glass and debris-free tracks. A common re-clean dispute area.
Decks, patios, and outdoor areas
Overview of all completed outdoor spaces.
All photos are sent via WhatsApp to Bonnie before you leave the property. WhatsApp timestamps are legally admissible evidence of when the job was completed to standard.
